heroHeadline: IFT-12 Starship Block 3 Slips to NET May 20 (T-1) as Musk Pushes IPO 'Pretty Soon' — S-1 Expected This Week
heroSubtitle: 8,778 days of SpaceX milestones — IFT-12 (Starship Block 3: Ship 39 + Booster 19 V3) slipped 24 hours to NET May 20, 2026 (22:30 UTC / 5:30 p.m. CDT, OLP-2, Starbase) for additional vehicle checkout time; as of May 18 the vehicle is fully stacked and no anomalies are reported. On May 18, Elon Musk appeared at the Samson International Smart Mobility Summit in Tel Aviv and told Bloomberg the SpaceX IPO needs to happen 'pretty soon,' adding the public S-1 prospectus could file 'this week.' Bloomberg simultaneously published 'SpaceX Needs Starship V3 Launch to Deliver Ahead of Planned IPO,' framing IFT-12 as the most consequential pre-IPO technical milestone — a successful Block 3 flight validates Raptor 3 performance and the V3 heat shield ahead of the targeted $1.75T–$2T+ Nasdaq valuation. The 5-for-1 stock split processing formally began May 18 (reducing fair market value from ~$526.59 to ~$105.32 per share; completion by May 22). CRS-34 Cargo Dragon C209 remains docked at the ISS Harmony forward port, delivering 6,500 lbs to Expedition 74 (docked May 17 at 6:37 a.m. EDT). SpaceX: 58 orbital missions in 2026, 611 total booster recoveries, 10,374+ Starlink satellites in orbit, 10M+ subscribers.
